methodology_note: P&C insurance holding company - standard FCF DCF is not used because operating cash flow is negative in multiple periods (FY2022: -$4,419.9m) and does not represent owner earnings. Instead this model compounds book value per share (BVPS) forward at a scenario growth rate net of the $15/share annual dividend, applies an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the realized 10-year trading range, and discounts dividends plus terminal value at cost of equity. See valuation_philosophy for full rationale.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr/5yr CAGRs (70%/102%) and OCF are highly misleading for FRFHF: EPS growth off a depressed FY2020 base ($6.29) and OCF swinging from -$4.4bn (FY2022) to +$6.6bn (FY2021) purely on investment mark-to-market noise are not representative growth signals. BVPS 5yr CAGR (21.4%) is rate-cycle boosted (2023-2025 record interest income + underwriting hard market) and should NOT be extrapolated forward; the 10-year BVPS CAGR (12.1%) and the softening-cycle guidance in the analysis JSON are used to anchor the base case instead, consistent with management's own long-run 15% target and cautious 2026 cycle commentary.
historical_growth.note_dividend_drag: BVPS growth is understated by ~1.2-1.3%/yr due to the $15/share annual dividend paid out of book value; management's stated 21% FY2025 BVPS growth is already 'adjusted for the dividend' (i.e., total value creation), which this model's growth_rates replicate by adding the dividend back before compounding.

base.description: Mid-cycle ROE ~11-12% net of dividend as the 2019-2025 hard market/rate cycle normalizes; underwriting stays profitable (CR ~93-96) but softens from FY2025 peak; interest/dividend income plateau/grow slowly as portfolio compounds even if rates ease. Exit P/B 1.10x, modestly above the 10yr average (1.07x) given structurally higher recurring interest income and the 2025 ratings upgrades (S&P AA-/A-) versus the pre-2022 rating profile.

bull.description: Rates stay higher for longer, combined ratio holds in the low-90s, India (Digit/Fairfax India) and Eurobank optionality convert to earnings, continued buybacks compound per-share value faster than the group level. Exit P/B 1.30x, below the 10yr max (1.51x) to stay conservative.

bear.description: Soft market pricing pressure drives combined ratio toward 97-100, a rate-cutting cycle compresses the $2.6bn interest/dividend income stream, and a large catastrophe year hits underwriting. Exit P/B 0.90x, near the 10yr low (0.71x in 2020) but not at the trough given permanently improved ratings/franchise quality.

sensitivity.row_axis: bvps_growth_rate_pct (avg of 5yr path, base path shifted uniformly)
sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows are the average annual BVPS growth rate (base 5-yr path of [12,11.5,11.5,11,11]% shifted -4/-2/0/+2/+4pp uniformly, average shown), columns are exit price-to-book multiple (0.9x-1.3x) applied to Year-5 BVPS. Cost of equity held at base case 9.5%. Field names (wacc_range/terminal_growth_range) retained for dashboard compatibility even though the axes here are BVPS growth and exit P/B, not WACC and perpetuity growth, per insurer-specific book-value-compounding methodology.

trip_conditions_checked: base upside > 100% with price in upper half of 10yr P/B range
sanity_check.diagnosis: Base-case intrinsic value of $1,490.68 implies a P/B of 1.19x on Q1-2026 BVPS ($1,250.14) and roughly 7.5x normalized EPS (~$200/share mid-cycle) - both comfortably inside the 10-year historical P/B band (0.71x-1.51x, avg 1.07x) and well below the peak multiple the stock has ever traded at. No FCF-DCF distortion risk exists here because the model is BV-compounding based, not OCF-based (OCF is negative in several periods and was explicitly excluded per methodology). Current price ($1,652, 1.32x BVPS) sits above the base case's implied fair multiple, consistent with a modest single-digit downside (-9.8%) in the base scenario and supports treating FRFHF as fairly-to-fully valued rather than deeply undervalued at current levels.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fairfax is a P&C insurance holding company where free cash flow / operating cash flow is not a meaningful proxy for owner earnings: OCF swings from -$4.4bn (FY2022, driven by mark-to-market bond losses and claims-reserve timing) to +$6.6bn (FY2021) purely on non-economic, non-distributable investment portfolio and float mechanics, with no relationship to intrinsic value creation. Management itself targets and reports against book value per share growth (stated objective: 15%/yr; realized 18.7%/yr since 1985 including dividends), not free cash flow. This model therefore uses a BOOK-VALUE-COMPOUNDING approach: (1) project BVPS forward using a scenario-specific compounding rate net of the $15/share annual dividend (consistent with how management itself reports BVPS growth 'adjusted for the dividend'), (2) apply an exit price-to-book multiple anchored to the realized 10-year P/B trading range (0.71x-1.51x) to derive a Year-5 terminal value per share, (3) discount dividends and the terminal value back to present at a COST OF EQUITY (not WACC, since this is a per-share equity-holder valuation, not an enterprise-value/FCF-to-firm calculation), and (4) derive an entry price consistent with a 15% CAGR target by discounting the Year-5 terminal value plus dividends reinvested at 15%. This mirrors the SUM.NZ underlying-profit and SRBK residual-income approaches used elsewhere in this project for businesses where GAAP/IFRS operating cash flow is not representative of distributable value.
valuation_philosophy.why_not_fcf_dcf: OCF was -$981m, -$3,075m, -$16.9m and +$496m across the four FY2022 quarters alone (net -$4,419.9m FY2022) purely from unrealized bond/equity mark-to-market moves flowing through the income statement under IFRS 17/9, and again went negative in Q1 2023 (-$1,125m) and Q4 2025 (-$1,298.6m). None of this reflects cash unavailable to shareholders - it reflects portfolio revaluation noise. A standard FCF DCF would either produce a negative/undefined valuation in loss years or require ad hoc 'normalization' of OCF that is really just re-deriving book value growth through the back door. Book value per share is the correct compounding unit for an insurer: it is what management targets, what rating agencies scrutinize, and what has historically driven the stock's total return.
valuation_philosophy.cost_of_equity_basis: Base case cost of equity of 9.5% reflects a AA-/A+-rated insurer (S&P upgraded core subs to AA- and debt to A- in 2025) with a diversified, decentralized global P&C/reinsurance franchise: risk-free rate ~4.3% (10yr UST) + equity risk premium ~4.5-5.0% + modest company-specific premium for holding-company complexity/opacity (partially offset by ratings quality and 40-year compounding track record). Bull case uses 9.0% (ratings/quality reduce perceived risk further); bear case uses 10.5% (softening cycle, catastrophe tail risk, succession uncertainty widen the discount rate).
